mizutani: Punjab plain Beas–Chenab; capital perhaps new Śākala
proposed: central Punjab; capital open (Asarur only if Sakala = Sanglawala Tibba; else near Sialkot, Majumdar)
basis: Cunningham ASR II pp. 191-203 (Asarur 15,600 ft round, moulded bricks; 15 li emended to 115), ASR V p. 113 and IX pp. 84, 103 (Takiya/Thakkiya as district names); Gujranwala 1883, Jhang 1884, Lyallpur 1905 echo ASR II; all depends on his Sangala; Bhandarkar CII 3 p. 9 reports Stein: Takka between Chenab and Ravi (editorial; no inscription names Takka)

proposed: Sialkot
basis: Majumdar, Dey: Sialkot; ASR II pp. 37-38, 191-99 surveyed Sangala hill (ruins c. 1.5 miles round; name and itinerary only, Sialkot not examined); Jhang/Lyallpur/Gujranwala repeat Cunningham; Vogel EI 16 p. 15 and Bhandarkar CII 3 p. 24 take Sialkot in passing (no inscription)

proposed: Chiniyari (Chine), 11 miles from Amritsar on the Sialkot road
basis: Cunningham ASR XIV pp. iv, 53-54 abandons his 1871 Patti for the lofty mound of Chine/Chiniyari (400 ft square, 46-50 ft high, large bricks); ASR XXI p. 134 old Vishnu image; Lahore 1883's Patti follows the superseded 1871 view

proposed: Jalandhar (kingdom incl. low hills Ravi–Simla)
basis: Kangra 1883 argues extent; Jalandhar 1884: old city c. 2 miles round, two tanks

proposed: Kulu; capital Nagar or Jagatsukh (Nast)
basis: Atkinson (Himalayan districts II 1884): Jagatsukh/Nast ancient seat of the Pala Rajas; name Kulanta still current; Kangra 1883 extent; Vogel AR 1903-04 pp. 263-64: Kullu = K'iu-lu-to accepted, 11th-c. Chamba plates name the lord of Kuluta (nothing on the capital)

proposed: Lahul
basis: Kangra 1883/1899 quote Cunningham; Atkinson mentions in passing; Jäschke's objection unaddressed; name: Lāhula in Tantrāloka 15.90 beside Kulūta, an Indian name, meets Jäschke (data/names/)

proposed: Ladakh
basis: Atkinson puts Mo-lo-so 2,000 li N of Lahul (consistent with Ladakh); no local evidence

proposed: Sarhind tract; capital perhaps Sanghol (excavated Kushan stupas and 27-cell monastery) rather than Sarhind
basis: no gazetteer hits; rests on Cunningham's emended distance; Rishi and Kuldip Singh IAR 1989-90 p. 93: Sanghol stupas S-2, S-3, monastery SGL-11, Kushan and Huna coins; excavators equate She-tu-to-lu with Sanghol (misreading ten sangharamas as stupas); no inscription, nothing of the 7th c. reported

proposed: Bairat, the only candidate; Xuanzang's monasteries not found there
basis: Cunningham ASR II pp. 242-48 (mound fits 14-15 li; Bijak hill platforms = two of the eight monasteries); Sahni AR 1935-36 p. 87 excavated Bijak-ki-pahari: one monastery, nothing after the 2nd c. AD, 'no evidence to corroborate this identification', one monastery 'in place of the eight' militates strongly against it (town mound unexcavated); distance from Satadru double (Majumdar), bearing off (Beal); Rajputana 1908, Alwar 1968 repeat

proposed: Mathura; ancient city = area within the Dhulkot mud rampart (over 3 sq km, Saka-Kushan), which includes the Katra
basis: ASR I pp. 233-39 (jail-mound Kunda-Suka tank), ASR XVII pp. 111-12 and XX pp. 31-32 (7th-c. city at the Katra, Jumna in the old channel); Muttra 1911: ancient city on the elevation SW; Muttra 1884, Mathura 1968: Buddhist remains at Mahaban; layout disputed; Vogel AR 1906-07 p. 140: Cunningham's and Growse's identifications 'signally failed'; ancient city = extensive elevation SW of the town, not the Katra (Katra = Yasa-vihara, extant 549-50); Muttra 1911 repeats Vogel's words; IAR 1954-55 pp. 15-16 (Katra trench: 'large part of the ancient urban settlement', two rings of mud ramparts) and IAR 1973-74 pp. 31-32 (Joshi and Srivastava: Dhulkot 'mud-fortification around the ancient city'), against Vogel's SW elevation

proposed: not located (unlocated)
basis: Cunningham moved it from the Katra (ASR I, III) to the old fort 1 mile E of the Katra (ASR XVII, XX), with no finds; Muttra 1911: Katra = Yasa Vihara (inscription), Kankali Tila Jain, proposals based on a wrong city site; Vogel AR 1906-07 p. 140: identifications based on a wrong city site inadmissible, Upagupta monastery and monkey tank 'still to be discovered'; Cunningham altered the text (west for east); Vogel's 'wrong city site' argument lapses (Katra inside the Dhulkot, IAR 1954-55, 1973-74), but nothing found; confidence lowered 2026-11-07: the place is unlocated, so no location can be high

proposed: Thanesar
basis: ASR II pp. 220-21: mounds 14,000 ft round (c. 4 miles), Asoka stupa = Madrasa mound NW; Karnal 1976 restates (3 miles = 20 li, Harsa-period bricks); answers Watters' distance objection; Sahni AR 1922-23 pp. 90-91: three mounds c. 3 miles round = 20 li, fort remains not earlier than c. 7th c. (14-in. bricks), probably founded by Harsa, W gate and 11-ft rampart located; stupa mound 3/4 mile NW undug (AR 1921-22 pp. 46-47); Karnal 1976 follows Sahni; Buhler EI 1 pp. 68-69 (Harsha's grant: ancestral seat Sthanvisvara = Thanesar); Pande IAR 1987-88 to 1989-90: Harsh-ka-Tila, Vardhana-period massive brick building, renovated fortification, 7th-c. inscription fragment; no Buddhist monument

proposed: Kurukṣetra (Nardak); Asthipur spot doubtful
basis: ASR II pp. 212-18 (400 li for 200; Asthipur pointed out W of the city), ASR XIV pp. 87, 98 (200 li each side; excavated Asthipura mound: unbaked-brick platform 364 ft, terracottas, no bones); Karnal 1884 (Ibbetson): radius; Karnal 1976: excavated mound 3rd-4th c. AD; Sahni AR 1921-22 pp. 46-47: region between Sarasvati and Drsadvati, mounds (Amin, Theh Polar, Pehoa) unexplored; Asthipur not discussed

proposed: near Gunana, 17 miles SSW of Thanesar; perhaps the Sita Mai monastery
basis: Cunningham (1871; ASR II pp. 226-27, tentative, no remains described); Karnal 1884 suggests the surviving Sita Mai monastery 4 miles from Gunana; name: 倶昏荼 = *Kohuṇḍa, shares no sound with Gunana; Gokaṇṭha/Govinda/Gominda break the key (data/names/)

mizutani: Sugh near Kalsi (Kalsi's coordinates; Dehra Dun district)
proposed: Sugh, c. 5 km E of Jagadhri, Ambala district
basis: Cunningham ASR I (near Paota/Topra; Kalsi rock within Srughna) revised in ASR II pp. 226-31 to Sugh (three forts, 19,000 ft = pilgrim's measure); ASR XIV p. 138 Kuninda coins most plentiful about Sugh; Ambala 1883 echoes ASR II; Mizutani's Kalsi coordinates/district reflect the abandoned ASR I view and need correcting; IAR 1963-64 p. 27 (Panjab Univ.); Chhabra and Suraj Bhan IAR 1965-66 p. 36: sealing 'Sugha' in 3rd-c. AD characters names the site; Malik and Acharya IAR 1995-96, 1998-99: nothing of Xuanzang's pillar or monastery; Ji p. 393 doubts Sugh on distance and size, but the 400 li run from the Gokantha monastery 100 li S of Thanesar, and size cannot outweigh the sealing

mizutani: where the Ganges enters the plain near Hardwar
proposed: near Hardwar
basis: no gazetteer hits

mizutani: E bank of the Ganges opposite Srughna
proposed: Bijnor tract E of the Ganges; capital perhaps Mandawar (unexcavated)
basis: ASR I pp. 248-51: Madawar mound half a mile square, large bricks, circuit fits 20 li, sub-sites by surface features; not excavated; Rohilkhand 1879 echoes ASR I; Bijnor 1908 calls them conjectural, notes stupa at Mordhaj

proposed: Mayapur, Hardwar
basis: ASR II pp. 232-35: name Mayapur, Brahmakund well; Meerut 1875, Saharanpur 1921/1981: old city traced locally to Raja Ben's fort, large-brick foundations, sculpture, coins; Watters' E-bank objection not tested; R. C. Majumdar EI 18: Jodhpur inscription V.S. 894 names Gangadvara and a king Mayura (conjecture)

proposed: Garhwal-Kumaon; capital the Brahmapura of the Talesvara plates, at or near Lakhanpur/Vairatpattan on the Ramganga; not Srinagar; Barahat a weaker alternative
basis: Atkinson 1884: Srinagar unimportant before 17th c., argues Barahat (50 miles due N of Hardwar, Aneka Malla trident); Almora 1981: Taleshwar plates issued from Brahmapura, capital Lakhanpur; Cunningham rejects Srinagar; Francke AR 1909-10 p. 106 in passing: Brahmapura = upper Ravi valley; Gupte EI 13: Talesvara plates (Almora) issued from Brahmapura, 'Lakhanpur or somewhere near it'; Vogel's Brahmor (Chamba) too far off

proposed: real; western Tibet: Nari-khorsum (Atkinson), Guge and Rudok, possibly E Ladakh (Francke)
basis: Atkinson 1884: Suvarṇabhūmi = Nari-khorsum; no Amazonian tradition in Katyur/Juhar/Niti, so across the passes; Chinese annals confirm the kingdom; Francke AR 1909-10 pp. 105-6: from the Sui-shu and Xuanzang's borders, the kingdom comprised Guge and Rudok, possibly E Ladakh; Leh multiple burials compared with the Chinese account of burial customs (analogy only)

proposed: Kashipur (Ujain fort, Bhim-gada mound); Dhikuli an unexcavated alternative
basis: ASR I pp. 251-55: Ujain fort c. 11,000 ft with suburb (text 12,000) but Cunningham 'unable to offer any identification whatever of the Buddhist remains'; Naini Tal 1904, Himalayan III 1886 echo; Atkinson 1884, Himalayan III 1886: Dhikuli Buddhist sculpture, local Bairatpatan tradition; Majumdar reports Fuhrer's Vairatpattan; Y. D. Sharma IAR 1965-66 p. 53, Iyengar IAR 1970-71 pp. 41-44: Bhim-gada mound, brick temple plinth 6th-8th c. (style), pottery AD 350-750, fill PGW to early medieval; identification accepted, no inscription, no Buddhist remains

proposed: Ramnagar (Ahichhatra)
basis: ASR I pp. 255-61: name Ahichhatr, fort over 3.5 miles round = 17-18 li, ravines, c. 20 temples dug, Chhatr stupa opened; Bareilly 1911/1965, Rohilkhand 1879 echo; Fuhrer EI 2 pp. 240-44: Pabhosa inscriptions of Ashadhasena of Adhichhatra (name only); Banerjee IAR 1964-65 p. 39: OCW-PGW-NBP-Kushan-Gupta sequence

proposed: Bilsar
basis: Cunningham ASR XI pp. 13-21 (1877) abandons his Atranji-Khera (ASR I, unvisited): Kumaragupta pillar inscriptions G.E. 96, 33-ft mound trenched (large bricks), mounds D-H = five deva temples (D excavated), circuit c. 1.75 miles, distances marched; Etah 1911 echoes ASR XI, Etah 1876 ASR I; Sahni AR 1922-23 pp. 93-95: Cunningham's identification 'unquestionable', site F excavated, Maitreya with Buddhist creed bought in the village; AR 1923-24 pp. 56-57: excavated ye dharma sealing establishes Buddhist monuments; stupa and monasteries unlocated; name: 毘羅刪拏 = *Vilaṣaṇa, fits the local Bilsanḍ (ASR XI) (data/names/)

proposed: Sankisa
basis: ASR I pp. 273-78: ramparts 18,900 ft = 20 li, coins, living Naga cult at Kandaiya Tal; ASR XI pp. 31-37: Pakna-Bihar monastery 6 miles E with three-staircase seals and Indo-Scythian inscription; Etah 1876, Farrukhabad 1911 echo ASR I; Kielhorn EI 7 p. 137: Harsha's Madhuban plate (AD 631) issued from the camp at Kapitthika = Kie-pi-tha = Sankisa (name attested, not site); Mani IAR 1995-96 pp. 89-91, 1996-97 pp. 138-42: rampart c. 6 km, PGW-Gupta, Maurya-Gupta monastery room W of the elephant capital; no naming inscription

proposed: Sankisa, by the Bisari Devi mound
basis: ASR XI p. 33: brick base of the elephant-capital pillar excavated due N of the Bisari Devi mound, monastery wall E of it; Pakna-Bihar staircase seals (ASR XI p. 37); Farrukhabad 1911 echoes only ASR I (no base found); elephant vs lion still unexplained; Mani IAR 1995-96, 1996-97: stupa mound under the Bisharidevi temple, monastery room by the elephant-capital site; nothing of the staircases or of the 7th c.

proposed: Kanauj
basis: ASR I pp. 279-92: Chota Ganga (Kali Nadi) = old Ganges channel, old city c. 3 miles long = 20 li, monuments not found; Farukhabad and Agra 1884, Farrukhabad 1911 echo; Hirananda Sastri EI 19, Sircar EI 32-34: Kanyakubja = Kanauj (Barah plate: Mahodaya camp distinct); Sinha IAR 1955-56 pp. 19-22: 40-ft city mound, PGW to late medieval

proposed: Newal, 2 miles N of Bangarmau (Unao district)
basis: Cunningham ASR XI pp. 48-52 abandons Nohbatganj (ASR I): Newal on the old Ganges bed, 19 miles from Kanauj, name, brick mounds with Vishnu and Buddha heads; Unao 1903 echoes ASR XI; Oudh 1877: probably Bangarmau; Majumdar, Dey

proposed: a site on the Ganges in the Fatehpur stretch (Aphui; or Cunningham's Kutia/Gunir or Patan-Bihar), unlocated; Ajodhya not excluded (Ajudhe coin)
basis: Cunningham ASR XI pp. 55-57: text crosses the Ganges southward from Newal, so Kutia/Gunir NW of Fatehpur or Patan-Bihar (replacing his Kakupur); ASR XVII pp. 99-100: Asni no Buddhist remains; keeps Ajodhya for Visakha; Fyzabad 1905: no Buddhist remains at Ajodhya; Oudh 1877 argues Ajodhya; Fatehpur 1916: Gunir mounds natural; Bajpai IAR 1970-71 p. 63: copper coin with legend Ajudhe (1st c. BC) from Ayodhya: the name at Faizabad's Ayodhya, not proof of Xuanzang's city

proposed: Partabgarh-Rae Bareli area on the Ganges; capital perhaps Tusaran Bihar (Partabgarh)
basis: Cunningham ASR XI pp. 57, 63-69: Daundia Khera nothing old; Tusaran Bihar on an old Ganges bed c. 30 miles NW of Allahabad, railing-type bricks, two stone stupas, Dalmau-Bihar 50 miles = 300 li; Oudh H-M 1877: Manikpur in Ayamukha; Oudh A-G 1877 rejects Daundia Khera; Mirashi EI 27: Kahla plates, a Kalachuri prince of Kalanjara conquered Ayomukha c. 700, = Partabgarh and Rai Bareli districts (editor's location)

proposed: Allahabad
basis: ASR I pp. 296-98 repeats Cunningham; Allahabad 1911: confluence lay further east (river shift)

proposed: Akshaya Vata, Patalpuri temple, Allahabad fort
basis: ASR I p. 297: Akshay Bat underground in the fort, due N of the Asoka pillar; Allahabad 1968, Muttra 1884 repeat; Allahabad 1911 doubts continuity of the temple

proposed: Kosam
basis: ASR I pp. 303-12 (name Kosambi-nagar, ramparts 23,100 ft = 30 li); Sahni AR 1921-22 (Meohar V.S. 1245, 'district of Kausambi'), AR 1923-24 (Kara V.S. 1093, Paras 'in the kingdom of Kausambi'; Bharhut abandoned); Pargiter EI 11 pp. 88-89 (V.S. 1621 record on the Kosam pillar names Kausambi; 7th/8th-c. records on it); Sahni EI 18 (Jayachchandra inscription 'final corroboration'); Hultzsch CII 1, Bhandarkar CII 3 (Kosambi edict pillar from Kausambi); G. R. Sharma IAR 1953-54 to 1966-67: rampart 3.5 miles, Ghoshitarama, SW stone palace c. 600 BC 'not unlikely' Udayana's (last phase 1st-2nd c. AD)

mizutani: monastery N of the E gate at Kosam (excavated)
proposed: the Ghoshitarama excavated by G. R. Sharma beside the E gate of Kosam
basis: Cunningham ASR I pp. 311-15 and XXI pp. 1-3: Ghosila's garden at Gopsahsa village SE of the fort (name only), monastery at Kosam Khiraj (railing pillars), Vasubandhu's chamber in the Tikri mound; no excavation; Mizutani's site rests on excavation; G. R. Sharma IAR 1953-54 to 1956-57: monastery identified 1951, Main Stupa c. 5th c. BC enlarged in the 3rd c. BC, tied by the excavator to Xuanzang's Asoka stupa (IAR 1955-56 p. 19); Buddhamitra inscription (Kanishka); occupied to the 6th c., destroyed under Toramana; naming record not quoted in the coded passages; Gopsahsa superseded

proposed: open: Sultanpur (distance only) or Bihar, tahsil Kunda (vihara name, remains; but c. 30 miles from Kosam and claimed for Hayamukha)
basis: ASR I pp. 312-15: Kosam-Sultanpur 109 miles = 700 li, but no stupa found; Sultanpur 1903: nothing at Mahmudpur/Sultanpur, kia = ka not ku; Partabgarh 1904's Bihar = Cunningham's Tusaran Bihar (ASR XI), his Hayamukha, far short of 700 li; name: 迦奢布羅 = Kāśapura; the key excludes Kuśa- and Kāśi- (data/names/)

proposed: unidentified; Ajodhya (Saketa) the only argued candidate, without the Viśākhā name link
basis: ASR I pp. 317-28: Sha-chi/Saketa legend, Dhanadeva and Visakhadatta coins only at Ajudhya, 30 miles N of Sultanpur, mounds as monuments (kept in ASR XI, XVII); Oudh 1877: the mounds are Ramkot bastions, identification impossible; Fyzabad 1905: no certain Buddhist remains; Faizabad 1960: Saketa not Ayodhya; name: XZ's fanqie 山格反 gives *Viṣaka, not Viśākha, so the Viśākhā/Sāketa name link fails (data/names/)
